paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the change in loss over iterations for different models. The x-axis is labeled "#Iteration" and uses a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 140,000 with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis is labeled "Loss" and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4 with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. There are six lines in the plot. The purple line, representing "Vanilla", starts at a loss of more than 3.4 and sharply decreases to approximately 2.7 at around 10,000 and gradually reduces to 2.45 by the end. The blue line, representing "StrmLLM (n=64)," starts at a similar loss of more than 3.4 and decreases more sharply at first till 2.9, reaching about 2.6 towards the end. The orange line, representing "SepLLM (n=64)", starts at more than 3.4 and decreases more sharply at first till 2.8, reaches approximately 2.52 at the end. The green line, "SepLLM (n=64, H)", begins more than 3.4 and decreases more sharply at first till 2.8, ends near 2.51, closely following the orange line. The red line, "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)", starts from more than 3.4 and steadily decreases to around 2.7, ends near 2.49. Lastly, the blue-violet line, representing "SepLLM (n=128)" also starts at more than 3.4 and decreases more sharply at first till 2.8, decreases to just above 2.5, with the final value just below the green line. All lines display a general trend of decreasing loss as iterations increase, with the most rapid decreases observed near the start. All the lines have minor fluctuations along the x-axis, and also, variance in a lighter shade. The blue line being slightly above all the other lines. There's a light green line at slightly greater than 0 from x-axis, parallel to y-axis. A legend is given top right.
